senses.gloss: (cmp. פָּגַל) to cut, mutilate; to damage, lessen; trnsf. (cmp. פָּסַל) to disqualify, unfit.
units: <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 21:3">Num. R. s. 21</cite> <he>כל הפּוֹגֵם את עצמו פיגם וכ׳</he> he who tarnishes his reputation discredits his family at the same time; Tanḥ. Pinḥ. 2; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 772">Yalk. Num. 772</cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:3:10">Y. Snh. II, 20ᵇ</cite> <he>פְּגָמָהּ הכתוב</he> the Bible text curtailed her name (<he>אביגל</he> for <he>אביגיל</he>, <cite ref="I Samuel 25:32">I Sam. XXV, 32</cite>).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 6">Gen. R. s. 6</cite> <he>חוזר ופוגם אותה</he> (not <he>אותם</he>) the text reduces her (the moon) again (calling her ‘the small light’).

<cite ref="Pesachim 105b:6">Pes. 105ᵇ</cite> <he>טעמו פְּגָמוֹ</he> as soon as he tasted it (the wine in the cup), he rendered it unfit (for a cup of benediction); a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="Q00046"><he>פָּגוּם</he></cite>; f. <he>פְּגוּמָה</he> &c.
<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 320">Sifré Deut. 320</cite> <he>בזוי ופ׳</he> contemptible and detested (<cite ref="Yevamot 63b:9">Yeb. 63ᵇ</cite> <he>משוקץ ומתועב</he>).
<cite ref="Ketubot 40b:7">Keth. 40ᵇ</cite> <cite ref="Q01377"><he>בעל פ׳</he></cite> if he had connection with an impaired woman (opp. <cite ref="U01327"><he>שלימה</he></cite>).

Y. Sabb. VI, 8ᵃ bot. כדי שלא … פ׳ (not פגימה) that it should not appear as if the right shoe were defective; a. e.—Esp. (law) to impair the legal value of a document by admitting a receipt on account (cmp. שׁוֹבֵר).
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 9:7">Keth. IX, 7</cite> <he>הפּוֹגֶמֶת כתובתה</he> a woman that impairs her marriage contract. expl.
<cite ref="Ketubot 87b:5">Ib. 87ᵇ</cite> <he>פוגמת כתובתה בעדים</he> if she states that she has received partial payment in the presence of witnesses.

<cite ref="Ketubot 87b:9">Ib.</cite> <he>פוחתת … היינו פוגמת</he> if a woman lessens the amount in her marriage contract (declaring that it has been made out for a larger amount than had been agreed upon) …, is it the same as admitting partial payment or not? Y. ib. IX, 33ᵇ <he>יורש שפ׳ אביו שטר חובו</he> an heir whose father had admitted partial payment on a note of indebtedness in his possession; <cite ref="Tosefta Shevuot 6:5">Tosef. Shebu. VI, 5</cite>.
<cite ref="Gittin 18a:11">Gitt. 18ᵃ</cite> <he>עד שתִּפְגּוֹם וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="G00649"><he>זָקַף</he></cite>; Y. Shebi. IX, beg. 39ᵇ; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be mutilated, diminished, impaired; to become defective, cracked, get out of order; to be discredited.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 6:1">Bekh. VI, 1</cite> <he>נִפְגְּמָה אזנו</he> if the ear of the first-born animal has become defective (lopped, bored through).
<cite ref="Arakhin 10b:38">Arakh. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>והיה קולו ערב ונפ׳</he> and the sound of the flute was sweet, but it became impaired.

<cite ref="Arakhin 10b:42">Ib.</cite> <he>אלו שני כלים … ונִתְפַּגְּמוּ וכ׳</he> those were the two implements that had remained from the first Temple, but they became defective and could not be mended; a. fr.
